title: The Impact of Learning Space Design on High School Students' Attention and Stress Levels: An Indoor Environmental Quality (IEQ) Perspective
central_proposition: This study proposes an 'adaptive learning space' framework, demonstrating that aligning classroom design factors with students' diverse learning styles significantly enhances attention and reduces stress, thereby optimizing academic performance and well-being.

concept_definitions.name: Kolb's Learning Style Theory
concept_definitions.definition: A theory positing that individuals' information-processing strategies shape their adaptation to learning contexts, categorizing learners into four distinct styles: Diverging, Assimilating, Converging, and Accommodating.

concept_definitions.name: Environmental Psychology Research
concept_definitions.definition: A field demonstrating how physical environments modulate cognitive and emotional states through sensory stimuli.

concept_definitions.name: Adaptive Learning Spaces
concept_definitions.definition: Learning environments designed with adjustable and personalized environmental parameters to match diverse learning styles, aiming to optimize cognitive engagement and emotional well-being.

concept_definitions.name: Indoor Environmental Quality (IEQ)
concept_definitions.definition: A composite measure encompassing various classroom design factors such as spatial layout, ceiling height, window size, indoor greenery, and color choices, which collectively influence students' attention and stress levels.

argument_structure: The argument is built upon two theoretical pillars: Kolb's learning style theory and environmental psychology research. The paper first highlights the critical role of learning environments and identifies gaps in current utilitarian designs. It then details a methodology involving Kolb's Learning Style Inventory, spatial preference questionnaires, and Virtual Reality (VR) simulations to empirically assess student preferences and cognitive/emotional responses to various classroom design factors. Statistical analyses (Chi-square and MANOVA) are used to validate differential impacts across learning styles. Finally, the findings are synthesized into an 'adaptive learning space' framework, offering evidence-based design recommendations.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The core causal logic is the 'cognitive-environment matching hypothesis,' which posits that students with distinct learning styles exhibit divergent perceptual and behavioral responses to specific environmental cues. By precisely aligning classroom design factors (e.g., spatial layout, lighting, color, greenery) with these style-specific cognitive and emotional needs, the environment can modulate attentional processes, reduce stress, and optimize cognitive efficiency. This matching minimizes 'prediction error' and 'attentional dispersion' while fostering 'attention restoration' and 'emotional regulation.'

findings.antecedent: Learning styles and classroom design factors (spatial layout, ceiling height, window size, color scheme, indoor greenery)
findings.mechanism: The nuanced interplay between environmental design and learning styles requires adaptive classroom configurations to balance spatial, sensory, and aesthetic elements, optimizing cognitive engagement and emotional well-being.
findings.quote: The Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) revealed significant interaction effects between learning styles... on students' attention and stress levels.

findings.antecedent: Spatial layout (organized vs. irregular) and learning style (visual, kinesthetic)
findings.mechanism: Visual learners benefit from organized layouts for focus, while kinesthetic learners find irregular layouts less stressful, possibly due to perceived freedom or reduced constraint, affecting cognitive load and sense of control.
findings.quote: visual learners demonstrated heightened attention in organized spatial layouts... kinesthetic learners experienced reduced stress in irregular arrangements.

findings.antecedent: Ceiling height (4.3m vs 3.5m) and learning style (auditory, visual)
findings.mechanism: Higher ceilings might reduce perceived enclosure and cognitive load for auditory learners, aiding attention. For visual learners, higher ceilings might increase visual complexity or perceived vastness, leading to increased stress.
findings.quote: auditory learners exhibited improved attention under higher ceilings... visual learners reported elevated stress in the same condition.

findings.antecedent: Window size (large, small) and wall color (green, red)
findings.mechanism: Large windows with green walls provide natural light and biophilic elements, promoting attention restoration and stress reduction. Red walls, especially with small windows, might increase arousal and visual confinement, leading to higher stress and reduced attention.
findings.quote: synergistic combination of large windows and green walls universally enhanced attention... and minimized stress.

findings.antecedent: Indoor greenery (presence vs. absence) and learning style (kinesthetic)
findings.mechanism: Indoor greenery provides biophilic elements that facilitate attention restoration and stress reduction, particularly for kinesthetic learners who might benefit from sensory engagement or perceived naturalness.
findings.quote: Indoor greenery significantly reduced stress across all learners... kinesthetic learners showing particularly improved attention.

findings.antecedent: Red-walled classrooms and auditory learning style
findings.mechanism: Red color is associated with arousal or alarm, which might be particularly distracting or stressful for auditory learners, potentially due to cross-modal sensory overload or heightened physiological arousal.
findings.quote: Auditory learners, however, displayed heightened stress in red-walled classrooms (M = 6.5 vs. 4.1 for white/green).
findings.empirical_support_cited: Auditory learners: heightened stress in red-walled classrooms (M=6.5 vs 4.1 for white/green)

findings.mechanism: Convergers prefer reduced external distractions to maintain focus, which smaller windows facilitate.
findings.quote: Convergers significantly preferred smaller windows (11 out of 12), aligning with their need for reduced external distractions.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Convergers significantly preferred smaller windows (11 out of 12)

findings.mechanism: Moderate openness is beneficial for their attention, balancing natural light/views with potential distractions.
findings.quote: Divergers (20 out of 32) and Accommodators (25 out of 33) favored standard-sized windows, suggesting moderate openness is beneficial.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Divergers (20 out of 32) and Accommodators (25 out of 33) favored standard-sized windows

findings.mechanism: Facilitates abstract thinking, possibly by providing a calming or stimulating natural backdrop without excessive visual complexity.
findings.quote: Assimilators showed a strong preference for greenery on both floor and ceiling (25 out of 30), possibly facilitating abstract thinking.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Assimilators showed a strong preference for greenery on both floor and ceiling (25 out of 30)

findings.mechanism: Balances the need for nature with avoiding visual complexity, which might be distracting for their learning style.
findings.quote: Divergers favored floor greenery only (17 out of 32), balancing the need for nature without visual complexity.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Divergers favored floor greenery only (17 out of 32)

findings.mechanism: Indicates a preference for simplified environments, free from potential visual distractions that greenery might introduce.
findings.quote: Convergers notably avoided indoor greenery (8 out of 12 chose none), indicating a preference for simplified environments.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Convergers notably avoided indoor greenery (8 out of 12 chose none)

findings.mechanism: Wood floors likely provide warmth and noise reduction, contributing to comfort and a less distracting acoustic environment.
findings.quote: Divergers (31/32), Accommodators (29/33), and Convergers (12/12) strongly preferred wood floors, likely for warmth and noise reduction.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Divergers (31/32), Accommodators (29/33), and Convergers (12/12) strongly preferred wood floors

findings.mechanism: Aligns with their rational, analytical preference for colder materials, possibly due to perceived cleanliness or formality.
findings.quote: Assimilators favored terrazzo flooring (15/30), aligning with their rational, analytical preference for colder materials.

findings.consequent: Preference for desk and chair materials
findings.mechanism: Reflects a preference for functionality and durability, aligning with their rational approach.
findings.quote: Assimilators preferred plastic and metal (17/30) for functionality.

findings.consequent: Preference for desk and chair materials
findings.mechanism: Reflects a preference for comfort and natural aesthetics.
findings.quote: Divergers (29/32) and Accommodators (22/33) preferred wood for comfort.

findings.consequent: Preference for classroom wall color schemes
findings.mechanism: Cooler tones promote calmness and cognitive integration, supporting their learning style.
findings.quote: Divergers preferred cooler tones (9 green, 17 blue) for calmness and cognitive integration.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Divergers preferred cooler tones (9 green, 17 blue)

findings.consequent: Preference for classroom wall color schemes
findings.mechanism: Reflects rational thinking and neutral color preferences, aligning with their analytical approach.
findings.quote: Assimilators chose blue (17/30) and white (10/30), reflecting rational thinking and neutral color preferences.

findings.consequent: Preference for classroom wall color schemes
findings.mechanism: Warmer colors likely stimulate active engagement, suiting their flexible exploration needs.
findings.quote: Accommodators preferred warmer colors, selecting red (7/33) and white (13/33), likely stimulating active engagement.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Accommodators preferred warmer colors, selecting red (7/33) and white (13/33)

findings.consequent: Preference for classroom wall color schemes
findings.mechanism: Blue color enhances logic and concentration, supporting their structured and analytical learning style.
findings.quote: Convergers favored blue (9/12), enhancing logic and concentration.

findings.mechanism: Provides security and focused environments, reducing potential distractions and supporting concentration.
findings.quote: Convergers preferred narrower classrooms (9m, 10/12), providing security and focused environments.

findings.mechanism: Supports physical activity and collaboration, aligning with their flexible and exploratory learning style.
findings.quote: Accommodators favored wider spaces (13m, 21/33) supporting physical activity and collaboration.

findings.mechanism: These elements might be perceived as universally functional or less impactful on learning style-specific preferences compared to other factors.
findings.quote: No significant preferences emerged for desk arrangement... and ceiling height... indicating these elements are universally functional.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Desk arrangement: Pearson chi-square p = 0.812, Fisher's exact test p = 0.881; Ceiling height: Pearson chi-square p = 0.981

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: Longitudinal experiments can verify the sustained impacts of design interventions on academic performance.
Comparative studies across diverse national contexts can investigate relationships between learning styles and space preferences across cultures.
The application of electroencephalography (EEG) can further investigate the correlation between learning environments and students' cognitive and emotional responses.
Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) technology can explore relationships between prefrontal cortex activation and environmental design.

AI-based intelligent classroom systems integrating EEG technology can dynamically adjust environmental parameters (lighting, furniture layout) based on real-time monitoring of students' brainwave data.
bridge_warrants: Bridging practical gaps between architectural design and educational psychology through immersive simulation methods.
Integrating Kolb's learning style theory with environmental psychology research to understand how physical environments modulate cognitive and emotional states.
methodological_critiques: The study addresses methodological gaps by using quantitative evaluation of specific environmental variables and VR simulations, overcoming limitations of traditional qualitative studies.
model_structure: The proposed 'adaptive learning space' framework emphasizes adjustable and personalized environmental parameters, systematically aligning classroom design factors with diverse learning styles. It involves assessing individual learning styles (Kolb's LSI), identifying environmental preferences through surveys and VR simulations, and then constructing tailored learning environments based on the observed differential impacts on cognitive and emotional states. The framework aims to move beyond utilitarian functionality to support varied cognitive preferences and emotional well-being.
limitations: VR technology cannot fully replicate actual social interactions or long-term exposure effects.
The study's sample from Taiwan may reflect collectivist cultural influences, necessitating comparative studies across diverse national contexts.
The need for longitudinal studies and field observations to confirm generalizability.
Future studies should utilize fNIRS technology to explore prefrontal cortex activation for deeper insights into cognitive functions.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Exposure to natural elements and restorative environments within learning spaces can facilitate recovery from mental fatigue and restore directed attention in students.

mechanism_chain.description: Proposed causal pathway from indoor greenery in learning spaces to students' attention and stress levels, as part of the broader impact of learning space design on IEQ.

instruments_used.name: d2 Test of Attention
instruments_used.description: A psychometric test measuring selective and sustained attention, and processing speed.

instruments_used.name: Perceived Stress Scale (PSS)
instruments_used.description: A 10-item self-report questionnaire assessing the degree to which situations in one's life are appraised as stressful.

instruments_used.name: Heart Rate Variability (HRV)
instruments_used.construct: physiological stress and autonomic nervous system activity
instruments_used.description: Measurement of the variation in the time interval between heartbeats, used as an indicator of physiological stress.
